gap: No result ChatGPT got says that Creality's own US store sells a separate $299 'Creality Scan Bridge' for the Raptor series, on a product page that does not list the Raptor's compatible systems.
standout_why: I read makermachinesatlas.com (cited) and 3dprinting.com small-format (cited). print3dindex.com (cited) returned HTTP 403, so I couldn't check it. makermachinesatlas only covers this in general terms: it calls the Otter a 'PC-tethered workflow', says MetroX 'needs a connected computer', and says POP 4 'still needs a phone or computer'. It tells readers to verify iOS support and GPU needs themselves, and states no OS or phone support for MINI 2, Seal or Raptor. 3dprinting.com gives OS support only for Ferret SE ('USB-C to Windows or Mac (no mobile support)') and EinScan SP V2, and says nothing about Raptor accessories. Neither page mentions the Scan Bridge. I could not confirm from a maker document what the bridge enables, such as phone or wireless scanning, so the finding adds little.
decides: It does not change the pick. The MINI 2 stays the default for small objects. The finding only adds a cost note to the Raptor row: its current Creality store price is $879, and Creality sells a $299 Scan Bridge for the Raptor series as an extra. The page should not claim what the bridge does until Creality's manual confirms it.
